title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INSPIRE PROGRAMME

Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau

Ministry of Science & Technology

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INSPIRE PROGRAMME

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
29 JUL 2026 4:44PM by PIB Delhi

Over the last five years, the Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research (INSPIRE) Programme of the department of science and technology has systematically nurtured scientific talent at different stages of the academic and research pipeline through its four major components. INSPIRE MANAK (Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge) promotes innovation and scientific creativity among students aged 10-17 years (Classes VI-XII) by encouraging them to develop and showcase original ideas and innovations. INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE) supports meritorious students aged 17-22 years pursuing undergraduate and postgraduate studies in natural and basic sciences by awarding 12,000 scholarships annually, each valued at

₹80,000 per year. INSPIRE Fellowship encourages outstanding graduates and INSPIRE scholars to pursue research through full-time Ph.D. programme(s) by providing financial support up to five years, including a fellowship of ₹37,000 per month as Junior Research Fellow (JRF), ₹42,000 per month as Senior Research Fellow (SRF), admissible House Rent Allowance (HRA), and an annual contingency grant of ₹20,000. INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship supports outstanding postdoctoral researchers, generally in the 27-32 years age group (with applicable age relaxations for reserved categories), through a five-year fellowship. Fellows receive ₹1,25,000 per month, an annual increment of ₹2,000, and a research grant of ₹35 lakh over the fellowship period.

The Government has undertaken a series of targeted interventions to significantly expand the reach and inclusivity of INSPIRE Programme, with a special focus on rural, remote, and aspirational districts across the country including Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency in Odisha and in the state of Rajasthan. These efforts include extensively deep dissemination of information through State Education Departments, District Education Officers, schools, and digital platforms; organization of awareness campaigns, orientation programmes, webinars, and capacity-building workshops for teachers and school authorities to improve the quality and reach of nominations. In addition, District, State, and National Level Exhibitions and Project Competitions (DLEPCs, SLEPCs, and NLEPCs) are hosted to identify, recognize and nurture innovative ideas among school students. To further strengthen the innovation ecosystem, mentorship programmes have been organized in collaboration with premier institutions such as IITs, NITs, IISERs, and other leading scientific organizations, providing selected students with guidance on   prototype   development, innovation, and   scientific research. These sustained efforts have a deep-reaching impact on the Society through participation in the INSPIRE programmes percolating across the country.

A growing number of students from rural and remote districts have benefited through innovation grants, mentoring support, and opportunities to showcase their scientific talent on national platforms. Collectively, these interventions have strengthened the scientific temper, the culture of inquiry, fostered grassroots innovation, expanded equitable access to science education, scholarly support, and research fellowships and strengthened young scientific talent represented from every region of the country.

The Government has been committed to promotion of the Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research (INSPIRE) Programme to encourage meritorious students to pursue higher education and research in sciences.
